data.name: APB Reloaded
data.detailed_description:
A cidade de San Paro é uma metrópole arrasada pelo crime no meio de uma revolução política. A introdução de uma lei de segurança originou a criação de guardiões da paz, os "Enforcers", vigilantes licenciados que vagueiam pela cidade com a intenção de parar os criminosos que os polícias não conseguiram. A fação destes guardiões da paz acredita que são uma força do Bem; a fação criminosa acredita que a cidade e a sua liberdade está sob ameaça
Mas quem tem razão? Os Criminosos ou os Guardiões da paz?
És tu quem decide a qual fação te juntas. Neste rápido jogo de ação PvP (jogador contra jogador, tu tens de lutar pela sobrevivência da tua fação, ganhando o respeito de poderosas organizações pelo caminho. Assim, as organizações vão-te fornecer armas, veículos e vestuários novos e exóticos que não só modificam a maneira como jogas mas o quão fixe pareces e soas enquanto o fazes.

Características Principais

  • Conquista a cidade quer como um guardião da paz ou um criminoso num mundo persistente.
  • Combate PvP (jogador contra jogador) frenético numa enorme cidade cheia de vida.
  • Personalização sem igual do jogador, vestuário e veículo.
  • 27 veículos únicos, desde jipes a carros de alta cilindrada.
  • Mais de 30 armas únicas, totalmente personalizáveis com inúmeras modificações.
  • Centenas de itens de vestuário e símbolos que tornarão a tua personagem completamente única.
  • Um sistema aprofundado e personalizado de música, onde podes criar os teus próprio temas.

data.short_description: The world’s first and premier Action MMO Third Person Shooter allows you to choose between two sides of the law. Play as Enforcer or Criminal, customize your gear for the task at hand and hit the streets and play how you want in a city filled with more action this side of a Hollywood blockbuster.

reviews.review:
[h1]APB Reloaded - A Game With Endless Potential and Absolutely No Idea What to Do With It[/h1]
[b]Recommended: NO - Unless You Enjoy Stockholm Syndrome With Extra Steps.[/b]

APB Reloaded started with one of the most unique and ambitious concepts in online gaming. Cops vs. criminals, open-world PvP, incredible customization, and a gameplay formula that genuinely had the potential to become something special.

Unfortunately, the only thing APB has consistently managed to improve over the years is [b]its ability to disappoint its remaining players.[/b]

[b]Over a decade later, APB is still stuck in the past.[/b] While the rest of the gaming industry moved forward, APB apparently decided that progress was an optional DLC.

Despite countless promises, attempted improvements, and questionable development decisions, the game has received virtually no meaningful engine improvements or major gameplay innovations that would make the experience feel fresh or enjoyable.

But don't worry, the annual holiday events are still here! Because nothing says [i]"the game is evolving"[/i] quite like recycling the same seasonal content while the core experience continues to deteriorate.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The New Player Experience: Welcome to the Meat Grinder[/h2]

Imagine downloading a new game, excited to learn its mechanics, only to get absolutely demolished by players with thousands of hours of experience, questionable aim, and enough accumulated equipment to fund a small military operation.

[b]That's APB Reloaded.[/b]

The game has an enormous problem with cheaters and an increasingly veteran-dominated player base. New players are thrown into an environment where learning the game feels less like progression and more like volunteering to become target practice.

And I'm saying this [b]as a veteran player.[/b]

The reward and progression systems are painfully outdated, offering very little incentive for newcomers to stick around. The matchmaking does practically nothing to create a fair learning environment, and the skill gap between beginners and veterans is often ridiculous.

The result? New players leave, veterans get frustrated, and the player base continues shrinking.

[i]But hey, at least the veterans can keep fighting the same 15 people they've been fighting since 2011.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]AI Anti-Cheat: Artificial Intelligence, Natural Stupidity[/h2]

And now we arrive at what I consider one of the biggest failures in APB's history: [b]the AI-powered anti-cheat system.[/b]

In my experience, this system has done more damage to the legitimate player experience than many of the problems it was supposedly introduced to solve.

Legitimate players can find themselves flagged for [i]"suspicious activity"[/i] and effectively shadowbanned, placed into separate matchmaking queues where finding a mission becomes nearly impossible.

Meanwhile, actual cheaters still appear to find ways around the system and effectively bypass it. It's genuinely impressive. We've somehow reached a point where an anti-cheat system can make the game feel less playable for legitimate players while failing to inspire confidence that cheating is being effectively addressed.

[b]Imagine being so good at fighting cheaters that you accidentally fight your own player base instead.[/b]

The introduction of this system has contributed significantly to the game's declining population. I can't verify exactly how many players were affected, but the impact on matchmaking and the experience of those caught in these queues is difficult to ignore. And the best part? Good luck figuring out whether you've been flagged, why you've been flagged, or what you're supposed to do about it.

[i]Apparently, the ultimate punishment for suspicious activity is being sentenced to play APB Reloaded without actually being allowed to play APB Reloaded.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]A Masterpiece of Wasted Potential[/h2]

APB Reloaded is one of those rare games that makes you genuinely angry, not because its original concept was bad, but because it was [b]so incredibly good.[/b] There is still nothing quite like it, and that's probably the saddest part.

It's a game that had everything it needed to succeed except consistent development, meaningful modernization, effective anti-cheat, balanced matchmaking, and a functioning new-player experience.
